policy.purpose: Small, inspectable training corpus for a character-level educational neural model. Entries teach terminology and epistemic discipline; they are not a substitute for retrieval or a proof checker.
policy.provenance: Archive entries are transcribed from the public AKSI Origin Archive. Mathematical entries are concise educational paraphrases with source links.
policy.warning: A model trained on this corpus learns character patterns, not verified reasoning. Sources and labels are metadata; the current character MLP does not ingest or reason over metadata.

entries.label: THEOREM
entries.text: Bayes theorem: posterior probability equals likelihood times prior probability divided by evidence probability, when the evidence probability is nonzero.
entries.caveat: The formula updates probabilities under a specified model; it does not make a prior or likelihood correct by itself.

entries.label: DEFINITION
entries.text: Shannon entropy measures the uncertainty of a discrete distribution: H(X) equals the sum of negative p(x) log p(x).
entries.caveat: Entropy depends on the probability distribution and logarithm base; it is not a direct measure of meaning or intelligence.

entries.label: DEFINITION
entries.text: Cross entropy measures the expected negative log probability assigned by a model to outcomes drawn from a target distribution.
entries.caveat: Lower test cross entropy means better probabilistic prediction on that test distribution, not necessarily truthfulness.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: Stochastic gradient descent updates parameters in the direction opposite an estimated loss gradient, scaled by the learning rate.
entries.caveat: A poor learning rate, noisy gradient, unsuitable model, or poor data can prevent useful learning.

entries.label: THEOREM
entries.text: Universal approximation results show that certain neural networks can approximate broad classes of functions under specified assumptions and sufficient capacity.
entries.caveat: Existence of an approximation does not guarantee efficient training, good generalization, factual knowledge, or small model size.

entries.label: THEOREM
entries.text: No-free-lunch results for optimization say that averaged across suitably unrestricted problem classes, no optimizer is universally best; performance depends on problem structure and assumptions.
entries.caveat: This is not the claim that all algorithms perform equally on every real task.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: SHA-256 maps input bytes to a 256-bit digest. Matching digests are useful for integrity checks, under the hash function's security assumptions.
entries.caveat: A digest alone does not prove who created the input, when it existed, whether it is true, or whether the signer is trustworthy.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: Ed25519 is a public-key signature scheme. A valid signature verifies under a public key; identity requires a trustworthy binding between that key and a person or service.
entries.caveat: A signature proves control of the corresponding private key under the cryptographic assumptions, not the truth of the signed statement.

entries.label: DEFINITION
entries.text: A Merkle tree combines hashes into a root hash and can provide a compact inclusion proof for a leaf under the tree's construction.
entries.caveat: An inclusion proof is meaningful only when the root is trusted or independently anchored.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: Train-test leakage happens when information from evaluation data influences model fitting or model selection, making evaluation overoptimistic.
entries.caveat: Keep held-out test data out of gradient updates and repeated tuning; use a separate validation set for model selection when possible.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: Reproducible machine-learning experiments record data versions, split seed, architecture, optimizer settings, software versions, metrics, and checkpoint hashes.
entries.caveat: A seed alone does not guarantee bit-for-bit equality across hardware, runtimes, or numerical libraries.

entries.label: LIMITATION
entries.text: Integrity is not truth. A cryptographic hash can detect changed bytes but cannot establish that the original claim is accurate.
entries.caveat: Evidence quality and independent verification must be evaluated separately.

entries.label: LIMITATION
entries.text: A language model can learn statistical patterns from text without verifying the claims it generates.
entries.caveat: Measure factuality with separate evidence-grounded benchmarks; next-character loss alone is insufficient.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: AKSI separates observation, inference, hypothesis, uncertainty, and opinion. State what an artifact shows and what it does not show.
entries.caveat: A claim becomes stronger only with evidence that directly supports it.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: A held-out test set estimates performance on unseen examples from a defined data distribution. It does not guarantee performance on every future input.
entries.caveat: Tiny or unrepresentative test sets give uncertain estimates.

entries.label: DEFINITION
entries.text: Generalization is performance on data not used to fit model parameters. Training performance alone cannot establish generalization.
entries.caveat: Distribution shift can make past test results a poor estimate of future behavior.

entries.label: ENGINEERING_PRINCIPLE
entries.text: For an AI claim, store the claim, evidence, source, assumptions, counterevidence, uncertainty, test procedure, and result separately.
entries.caveat: A structured record improves auditability but does not automatically make its contents correct.

entries.label: LIMITATION
entries.text: A tiny character-level neural network predicts characters from short contexts. It is not a modern transformer language model and should not be presented as one.
entries.caveat: Its main value is a transparent training demonstration and a baseline for controlled experiments.
